newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS ITALY'S SECOND GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS ITALY'S SECOND GOLD.

text.p: Deborah Compagnoni became the first Italian Alpine skier ever to defend a world title on Sunday when she won the women's giant slalom for her second gold of the world championships.
Compagnoni, who won the giant title at the 1996 championships in Sierra Nevada and the slalom here on Wednesday, clocked two minutes 39.19 seconds down the Sises 2 piste.
She had led by 0.73 seconds after the first leg.
Switzerland's Karin Roten, runner-up to Compagnoni last year, was again the silver medallist in 2:39.99, 0.80 seconds behind.
It was her second medal of the championships after she took bronze in the slalom.

Leila Piccard was a surprise bronze medallist in 2:40.95, coming from 12th place after the first leg to take France's first medal and make up for the disappointment of men's downhiller Luc Alphand who crashed on Saturday.
Austria's Anita Wachter, chasing the eighth medal of her career, had been third after the first run but failed to stay in the medal positions and finished fourth.
Double Olympic champion Compagnoni now has the same number of career gold medals -- five -- as compatriot Alberto Tomba.
